title: Stock Market Today Highlights: Stock markets tumble on oil price spike, foreign fund outflows; Sensex drops 548 points - The HinduBusinessLine
text:

Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Highlights: Erasing opening gains, the 30-share BSE Sensex tanked 547.65 points, or 0.76%, to settle at 71,924.68. The 50-share NSE Nifty dropped 157.10 points, or 0.70%, to end at 22,363.35.

From the 30 Sensex firms, ITC, Tech Mahindra, Hindustan Unilever, Larsen & Toubro, State Bank of India and Tata Consultancy Services were among the major laggards. Bharat Electronics, Mahindra & Mahindra, Kotak Mahindra Bank and HCL Tech were among the major winners.

Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, jumped 1.14% to $105.8 per barrel.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) offloaded equities worth ₹3,568.90 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.

The Indian rupee rose 0.99% versus the U.S. dollar to ‌95.77, after the central bank took steps to temper dollar demand in the ‌spot and derivatives markets, with likely intervention through dollar sales adding ⁠to the gains.

Despite prevailing negative sentiment around the Nifty 50, September’s mutual fund data highlights the resilience of India’s domestic investor base amid market corrections and global macroeconomic uncertainties. Equity-oriented mutual funds attracted net inflows of ₹38,307 crore during the month, with investor flows remaining remarkably strong in the small- and mid-cap segments. Small-cap funds attracted ₹9,039 crore, while mid-cap funds garnered ₹7,835 crore, his continued participation suggests that retail investors remain positive on India’s long-term growth opportunity, particularly across the mid- and small-cap segments.

Notably, monthly SIP contributions rose to a record ₹32,490 crore, reinforcing the trend of disciplined investing despite market volatility. Total Equity-oriented mutual fund inflows increased approximately 31% month-on-month, reflecting sustained investor participation even as market sentiment remained subdued.

The strength of flows across equity categories suggests that retail investors are continuing to invest through the correction rather than retreating from equities.Passive investing also remained strong, with equity ETFs attracting ₹9,960 crore, while gold ETFs received ₹4,451 crore, indicating continued interest in diversification.

Overall, the data suggests that negative market sentiment has not materially dented investor appetite for small- and mid-cap opportunities. Investors should remain disciplined, diversify across market capitalisations and align equity exposure with their investment horizon rather than chase recent flows.

The RBI’s response is calibrated but firm. The announced ₹25,000 crore open market bond sale will absorb surplus liquidity, while the higher daily CRR maintenance requirement will tighten banks’ liquidity management. Separately, targeted foreign exchange measures are easing pressure on the rupee, which strengthened approximately 1% to around 95.76 in early trading.

These measures redirect dollar demand away from the spot market rather than eliminate it, so lasting currency stability will still depend on crude prices, capital flows and the broader dollar trend.
